newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes firmer, Australian grades trade firm.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes firmer, Australian grades trade firm.

text.p: Crude oil prices in Asia were firmer on Tuesday, spurred higher by an overnight rally in London and New York crude futures.
Early London prices Tuesday were lower than day-earlier levels, although Brent edged into firmer territory later.
November paper Tapis rose to $24.95/$25.05 after December was valued at $24.65/$24.75, pushing assessments for wet November Tapis crude oil above $26.00 per barrel.
However, most Tapis appeared already sold for November. A producer has been marketing December barrels since last week after selling more than 2.5 million barrels in November.
Traders said the producer had a small parcel of Tapis left to sell for November. Other light sweet grades traded in line with the firm light sweet market.

Two majors sold a combined 450,000 barrels of early December Thevenard to a Korean refiner for Tapis quotes plus $1.80 and a producer sold 300,000 barrels of Challis to a U.S. major at Tapis quotes plus $1.85. Both deals were in line with relative values to Tapis, traders said.
A mid November Kutubu -- the final availability for the month -- was sold by a major to another major at Tapis quotes plus 27 cents. The barrels stayed in Australia.

A Japanese trading house kicked off the December Gulf market, selling 500,000 barrels of Qatar Land at QGPC +20 cents to a Korean refiner. The same refiner took 900,000 barrels of Masila from traders at dated Brent -$1.20/$1.30.
A December Murban was said done at ADNOC +35 cents into Japan.
Two Japanese traders sold 450,000 barrels each of November Bach Ho at OSP +9 cents. A U.S. major and a Japanese refiner were the recipients.
